ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Dominantly low-intensity (black) surface area (approx. 85-90%) with high-contrast (white) localized intensity clusters (approx. 10-15%) primarily representing scar tissue and speckling.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: High-intensity white circular rings (rosettes) are distributed throughout the lower-mid regions of both lobes. Dense white punctate mottling is visible along the lower margin near the central fluke junction. The remaining area is a contiguous low-intensity black field.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: V-shaped median notch with an approximate internal angle of 48 degrees and a depth-to-width ratio of 0.25 relative to the central fluke chord.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: High-frequency, irregular serrations across the entire trailing edge boundary. Significant peak-to-valley pixel amplitude observed on the distal third of both lobes, creating a jagged profile against the high-intensity background.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Symmetrical convex sweep along the trailing edge, transitioning to a slight taper at the distal tips.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Extensive detection of white circular and semi-circular ring clusters ranging from 10 to 40 pixels in diameter. High density cluster observed in the lower-left quadrant of the left lobe.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Faint diagonal linear disruptions visible on the right lobe distal region, appearing as higher-intensity scratches against the black background.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Extensive circular scarring (rosettes) consistent with parasitic or predatory interactions across the majority of the ventral fluke surface; significant raggedness and potential tissue loss on the distal right tip.
other_distinctive_markers: High-intensity white stippling field concentrated at the lower-central margin where the fluke lobes converge.
